title: The SQL connector reads PostgreSQL: the read-only step no longer runs on a streaming connection
request: The owner asked whether DCLab can run SQL for its users, then for the address of DCLab's own database to test with, and how to connect it.
spec: A query or a table read from a PostgreSQL connection loads its rows into a draft, in a transaction declared read only; a write, an INTO or a second statement is still refused.
plan: connect the local dclab_dev database as a connection and read through the draft route
find why every query is rejected
order the read-only declaration before streaming
a PostgreSQL test that fails on the old order

decisions.decision: The fix is the order of two calls, not a different way of streaming
decisions.why: a streaming connection sends every statement as a cursor query, and SET TRANSACTION cannot be one; declared first, the read itself can stream as before

decisions.decision: The regression test uses the PostgreSQL test database and is skipped without one
decisions.why: SQLite, which every other connector test uses, has no read-only declaration and no cursor query, so it could never show this defect

change: dclab_rnd/connectors/db.py (SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY before stream_results); tests/test_connectors.py (PostgresReadTests).

findings.defect: On PostgreSQL every table and every query was refused as a syntax error, so the connector could not read any PostgreSQL database
findings.scenario: DCLAB_DB_DCLAB=postgresql+psycopg://user@/dclab_dev, then any SELECT through the draft's database route
findings.cause: fetch switched the connection to stream_results first and then ran SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY, which the driver sent as a cursor query that PostgreSQL refuses; only SQLite was ever tested
findings.fix: the declaration runs first and the connection streams afterwards

measurements.name: PostgreSQL read through the draft route
measurements.gate: a live read of the local development database
measurements.result: a grouped query and a table read loaded rows into a draft; a DELETE and two statements were refused; the transaction reports read only
limits: the database user is a superuser, so the word check is the only other guard
one local PostgreSQL and one driver (the newer psycopg); the older driver and other dialects were not run

outcome: A PostgreSQL connection now loads rows; the new test fails on the old order and passes on the new.
lessons: a safety feature that only one database dialect has needs a test on that dialect: the SQLite tests passed while PostgreSQL never worked
risks: connections are defined on the server and shared by every user of it
no query time limit was found
the word check may refuse a column named like a write word; not tested
